title: Jill Watson virtual teaching assistant in a Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence course
system_purpose: Augment human teaching staff by answering routine questions and supporting the online discussion forum for Georgia Tech OMSCS 7637 Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence
decision_impact: The system determined whether and how routine course information was delivered while human teaching staff remained responsible for instruction and non-routine support
affected_groups: online artificial intelligence students;instructors;teaching assistants;students needing non-routine clarification
verified_facts: Georgia Tech reports that Jill Watson operated in different offerings of OMSCS 7637 Knowledge-Based Artificial Intelligence from Spring 2016; about 750 students had interacted with versions of the system, and the Spring 2017 version autonomously handled introductions, weekly announcements, and routine frequently asked questions.
reported_harm: No realized student harm was reported in the source; a foreseeable hazard is that an autonomous response outside its validated routine-question scope could mislead a student or delay access to appropriate human clarification.
quantitative_evidence: The report gives an approximate cumulative scale of 750 students across offerings from Spring 2016 through the latest Spring 2017 offering, but it reports no causal learning-gain or error-rate estimate.
limitations: This is a first-party technical report, its publication metadata gives only a year, and the described system focused mainly on course interaction and routine questions rather than generative tutoring across the full introductory AI curriculum.

title: CodeHelp guardrailed LLM assistant in computer and data science
system_purpose: Provide always-available programming help without directly revealing solutions
decision_impact: The assistant selected guidance for student coding problems while instructors and teaching assistants retained responsibility for teaching and escalation
affected_groups: first-year computer and data science students;instructors;teaching assistants;students who find it difficult to formulate a help request
verified_facts: The peer-reviewed Koli Calling paper reports that CodeHelp was deployed for 12 weeks in a first-year computer and data science course with 52 students and used prompting guardrails intended to guide students without directly producing solutions.
reported_harm: Students reported cases where CodeHelp misunderstood a question, gave confusing or unrelated advice, or introduced concepts not yet taught; a small number of survey responses also raised over-reliance, while the paper did not establish a verified adverse academic outcome.
quantitative_evidence: Of 52 enrolled students, 45 completed the optional incentivized survey; the paper reports that 14 respondents described difficulty using the tool, five mentioned content not covered in class, and three responses indicated over-reliance concerns.
limitations: This was one small course, the survey was optional and incentivized, the instructor was also an author, and self-reported themes do not prove causal effects on learning or generalize automatically to a Vietnamese introductory AI course.

title: Non-native writer bias and institutional withdrawal of AI detection
system_purpose: Classify whether submitted student writing was likely generated by AI
decision_impact: Detector flags could influence instructor scrutiny and potentially feed academic-integrity investigation or disciplinary workflows
affected_groups: non-native English writers;students subject to integrity review;instructors
verified_facts: A peer-reviewed study tested seven GPT detectors on 91 human-written TOEFL essays and 88 US eighth-grade essays and found a large difference in misclassification; Vanderbilt separately reported disabling Turnitin AI detection after reviewing reliability transparency bias and privacy concerns.
reported_harm: False AI-authorship flags create a foreseeable risk of false accusation, dignity loss, unequal treatment, and privacy exposure; the cited sources do not establish a regulator finding or a verified count of disciplinary outcomes.
quantitative_evidence: Across the seven detectors the TOEFL essays had a 61.3% average false-positive rate; all detectors flagged 19.8% unanimously and at least one detector flagged 97.8% of the 91 essays.
limitations: The peer-reviewed test concerned selected 2023 detectors and datasets rather than AIGuide or Turnitin specifically; Vanderbilt's withdrawal is a first-party operational decision, so this adjacent assessment case is used only to support the product's no-grading and no-discipline boundary.
